request.spec:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now name other people on the sheet as patrons, one at a time from their own row, and each row shows their patrons and backing. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it behaves**
- **Adding a patron:** each person's row has a patron picker and an "Add patron" button. The picker lists everyone else on the sheet, so a person can never pick themselves. Picking someone who is already their patron is refused by the server: the row shows `person-patron-error`, and nothing is written to the store or the audit file. Changing the picker clears the error.
- **Audit record:** a patron that goes through writes `PATRON_ADDED sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<name> patron=<patron name>`.
- **Display:** `person-patrons` shows the patron names sorted and joined with ", ". `person-backing` adds up the patrons' due-totals, skips any that are n/a, and shows 0.00 when there are no patrons.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new `patron` table (`V19__patron.sql`). Each person–patron pair is its own row, keyed so the same pair can't be stored twice.
- **Server:** a new `patron` package with two endpoints. `GET /api/sheets/{sheet}/patrons` lists them. `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/people/{person}/patrons` takes the patron's person id, adds it, and answers with the updated list. A refusal is a 400, through its own escalation handler.
- **Front end:** a new `features/patrons/` column on the person row. Backing is worked out in the browser using the same due-total function as the `person-due-total` column, so the two always agree, including for held people.

Two choices the request left open:
- Retired people still appear in the picker and count toward backing, the same as anyone else on the sheet.
- I kept patrons out of the `Person` record and its endpoints; they're a separate list the person row looks up.
